description:
kopitiam-pdf has NO /Encrypt support at all - no crypt module, no handling anywhere. Any encrypted PDF fails to open.

Found 2026-08-31 SGT on a real government form the maintainer handed kpdf. Its dict: /Filter /Standard, /V 4, /R 4, /Length 128, /StmF /StdCF, /StrF /StdCF, /CF << /StdCF << /CFM /AESV2 /Length 16 >> >>, /P -1052. That is AES-128-CBC under the standard security handler.

Almost certainly an EMPTY USER PASSWORD with owner restrictions - the ordinary shape of a fill-in-but-do-not-edit form, which is why every other viewer opens it with no prompt. So the common case needs no password UI at all: derive the key from the padded empty password and go.

DONE ALREADY (this session): detection + an honest error. Before it, the failure surfaced as 'corrupt object stream (134 0 R)' - the stream is not corrupt, it is ciphertext, and inflating ciphertext produces exactly the garbage a corruption check catches. PdfDocument::open now refuses with ErrorKind::Unsupported naming the scheme: 'encrypted PDF (/Standard, V4 R4, AESV2) -- decryption is not implemented yet'. 3 tests.

STILL TO DO - the actual handler:
* Algorithm 2 key derivation (7.6.3.3): pad the password to 32 bytes, MD5 over pad + /O + /P (LE) + first /ID element, and for R>=3 iterate MD5 50 times over the first /Length bytes.
* Algorithm 6 user-password check against /U, so an empty password is verified rather than assumed.
* Per-object key: MD5 of key + obj num (3 bytes LE) + gen (2 bytes LE), plus the literal 'sAlT' bytes 0x73 0x41 0x6C 0x54 for AESV2. Cap at 16 bytes.
* AES-128-CBC decrypt with the leading 16 bytes as IV; RC4 for /V 1,2 and /CFM /V2.
* Apply to STREAMS and STRINGS both, and NOT to the /Encrypt dict itself, /ID, or an unencrypted-metadata setup. Object streams decrypt at the stream level - contained objects must NOT be decrypted a second time, which is the classic double-decrypt bug.
* /V 5 /R 6 (AES-256, SHA-256 based, PDF 2.0) is a separate later job.

DEPENDENCIES - needs the maintainer's call under the Pure Rust Core hard rule. RustCrypto has exactly-fitting pure-Rust crates: aes, cbc, md-5, rc4, sha2. All actively maintained, MIT OR Apache-2.0 (compatible with AGPL-3.0-only), no C toolchain, small and precisely scoped. The hard rule says prefer an existing crate over hand-rolling, and hand-rolling crypto is a bad idea besides. Four or five new deps in the core crate is still a maintainer decision, hence asking rather than assuming.

Payoff: unlocks a whole CLASS of documents, not one file. Government and company forms are very often owner-restricted this way.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
DONE for reading. Standard security handler implemented in crates/kopitiam-pdf/src/mupdf/crypt.rs (R2-R4, RC4 + AES-128-CBC), wired into PdfDocument. The maintainer's MOM work-pass form now opens: 10 pages, 90 form fields, all embedded fonts resolving, ~50ms/page render.

Deps (maintainer approved): aes 0.8, cbc 0.1, md-5 0.10, rc4 0.1 - PINNED to the versions already in the tree transitively via hayro/lopdf, NOT the newest published. aes 0.9/cbc 0.2/md-5 0.11 sit on cipher 0.5 + digest 0.11 and would put a second copy of each primitive in the build. cargo tree confirms one version of each.

Wiring, and the two traps:
* Streams decrypt at PdfDocument::stream_raw_num - the single chokepoint for raw bytes - BEFORE any /Filter. Decrypt-then-inflate; inflating first is what produced 'corrupt object stream'.
* Strings decrypt ONLY on the Uncompressed (direct object) path. An object parsed out of an object stream was encrypted as part of that stream and is already plaintext; decrypting it again yields garbage that still parses. The Compressed arm deliberately leaves strings alone.
* /Encrypt's own /O and /U are never decrypted (encrypt_obj_num guards it explicitly rather than relying on cache-population order).

RC4 needed a runtime-length key but the crate makes it a compile-time generic, so rc4_apply dispatches over the 12 sizes the spec permits rather than hand-rolling the cipher.

17 crypt tests + 3 xref tests. Includes a forward/backward consistency check: compute /U from a key via Algorithm 4/5, then verify it back through user_password_matches, for R2/R3/R4, and confirm a wrong password is rejected.

STILL MISSING, and now guarded: we can DECRYPT but not ENCRYPT. add_ink_annot and set_field_value now refuse on an encrypted document with ErrorKind::Unsupported. Without that guard they would append plaintext objects, producing a file that still opens in kpdf (we read our own plaintext back through a decryptor that mangles it) and is unreadable everywhere else - silent corruption of someone's real form. Write support is a separate job, filed separately.

Also not implemented: /V 5 /R 6 (AES-256, SHA-256 based, PDF 2.0). Refused by name.

title: kopitiam-pdf: implement the standard security handler (encrypted PDFs)
